verdict.rationale: Discord documents a public REST API with bot-token and OAuth2 authentication, versioned endpoints (v10/v9 available, with deprecation status and a change log), and a Gateway WebSocket API for events. An official machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 spec is also published on GitHub, and agent-friendly llms.txt and markdown docs are reachable. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the API, and a stable (non-preview) OpenAPI spec, since the published spec is marked preview and the docs-site OpenAPI paths return 404.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: 1. Using a bot token... 2. Using an OAuth2 bearer token
Discord exposes different versions of our API. You should specify which version to use by including it in the request path like https://discord.com/api/v{version_number}
The Gateway API lets apps open secure WebSocket connections with Discord to receive events about actions that take place in a server/guild
The official discord/discord-api-spec repository publishes a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document
